text: What to do if your girlfriend is going to see her female friend and then you find out there will be another guy there? This bothers you but you are not sure how to handle the situation. This is a question I received from one of my subscribers. Let's read it. Hi dude, I was wondering if you could give me some advice on what to do because I can't get it off my mind. My girlfriend was originally inviting her friend around the drink on New Year's home alone and her friend has invited a guy who is a few years older than both of them. I'm guessing they're both going to just view him as a friend but I don't even know who this guy is. Plus my girlfriend's friend doesn't like me either that's why I didn't offer myself to go because I wanted to avoid any awkwardness because I've argued with her before. I'm just worried what the guy might do if they are all going to be drinking. Is it stupid of me to not go because of that? Okay guys, first of all, if you have a question about dating or you have some interesting relationship situation you can send me a direct message here or over the telegram. But this was my answer. Look, I'll be straight with you. If she's your girlfriend and this is a serious relationship then you are one unit. You and her together. So first question. Why does she have a friend who doesn't like you and why would she ever choose a friend over you? Reverse the situation. You have a friend and you introduce him to your girl and he says I don't like her. If he has good reasons, so the friend has good reasons, then why are you even with that girl? If he has no real reason then why is this guy even your friend after saying that about your girl? Second point. Did your girlfriend even invite you? If there are other people coming and she didn't invite you, that's already weird. And if she knows she's going without you and her friend brings another guy, she should say look I'm not comfortable meeting other guys without my man. Either we meet just us two or I bring my man. Or she just doesn't go at all. At the end of the day, if something is bothering you, you talk to your girl and explain it clearly. She either understands and you find a compromise or, and this is a hard truth, you have to accept that you deserve better. And as hard as it is, you should be the one to end it. Then he wrote this. She said I can come if I want but she is still going to bring the guy because he didn't get invited to a party so she feels bad for him but I'm not sure if I'm spending it with my family or not so I'm not sure whether to give up my new years with my family just so I can watch over this guy or not. I would like to think her offering me to come is a good sign but it's the guy I don't trust. The only way to find out is to just wait and if she does try anything just leave because I feel like I'm already acting as if the night has already happened if you know what I mean. I tend to overthink with stuff like this. To this, this was my answer. It is not overthinking, it is normal reaction a lot of men would have. If you plan to spend your holidays with family, you do not change your plans because of the situation. Bottom line, it is simple. You tell her how you feel about the situation, you explain it to her and either she sees your point and you find a compromise, for example, maybe she joins you on your celebration or you understand that you are probably not that important for her, then I suggest you end it. And then I think he wrote thank you blah blah. Yeah, that's about it. Thanks guys and bye.
